items.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says neocloud stocks rallied Monday on the return of Jensen Huang to NVIDIA. At 1:30 p.m. Eastern, Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) and CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) were each up 21%, IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) was up 25%, TeraWulf (NASDAQ: WULF) was up 13% and Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) was up 12%. Leading ETFs showed software up closer to 4% and semiconductors up 13%. Bleeker also pointed to two company-specific items. The New York Times reported that Anthropic's demand is so large that SpaceX needs new data centers by October to fill its orders. On Friday, Oracle said it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Bleeker notes Nvidia helped build neoclouds with funding, technical expertise and chips. He calls it a one-day win. Nebius is down 38% over the past month, CoreWeave 12% and Oracle 10%. Over six months Nebius is down more than 50%, Oracle 40% and CoreWeave 55%. Bleeker names three drivers of the selloff: higher rates and wider credit default swaps, political worries after the midterms, and Huang's removal. Only the last has reversed. Going forward, watch the Fed's rate path and how politics affects project locations such as Texas.

items.headline: Palantir Rips 10% to Lead Software Stocks. Cloudflare and ServiceNow Also Join ‘Jensen Rally’
items.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%. Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.
